title: India's I4C warns of social media job offers that lure Indians into Myanmar cyber-scam compounds
date_note: The source pages give only their publication day, 26 November 2026.
geo_basis: Agency (I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs); the report is datelined New Delhi
summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), which works under the Ministry of Home Affairs, issued an alert on social media recruitment scams, as reported by ANI. It describes a Chhattisgarh woman who answered a Facebook job advert for Bangkok and was allegedly taken to Myanmar, where her passport was confiscated and she was forced into online investment scams until a raid freed her.
plain: India's cyber crime agency warns that fake job offers on social media have led Indians to be taken to Myanmar and forced to run online scams.
exec: I4C, India's cyber crime coordination centre, is warning about social media recruitment scams that lead to forced work in online scams in Myanmar.
action: I4C advises verifying the credentials of foreign employers, recruitment agencies and job offers before applying or travelling, and reporting suspicious recruitment activity to authorities.
attack: Fake job offers on social media

sources.name: Deccan Chronicle (ANI): I4C Warns of Social Media Job Scams Luring Indians Into Myanmar Cyber Slavery
Asian Age (ANI): I4C Warns of Social Media Job Scams Luring Indians Into Myanmar Cyber Slavery

validation.note: Deccan Chronicle and Asian Age both carry the same ANI report, so one publisher; I4C's own page was not read.
